summary: Cloud-native storage abstraction — one interface for local files, S3 (any flavour), HTTP, and more, with transparent compression, encryption, and cross-backend transfers.
the_vision: Data lives everywhere — local disks, S3 buckets, HTTP endpoints, R2, MinIO, B2, and eventually GCS, Azure, and SFTP. The access patterns are the same but every backend demands its own code. mountainash-transport provides a single interface where backends declare their capabilities through protocols, compression and encryption compose as transform pipelines, and path-driven dispatch routes to the right backend automatically.

what_it_makes_possible.capability: Read from anywhere with one call
what_it_makes_possible.essence: read_bytes('s3://bucket/file.gz'), read_bytes('https://api.example.com/data.csv'), read_bytes('/tmp/local.parquet') — same function, same interface. URL scheme detection routes to the right backend. Transform pipelines decompress and decrypt transparently.

AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Backblaze B2, S3 Express — all S3-compatible, all slightly different. One settings class with a flavour field handles the variations. Connect to any S3-compatible service with the same code.

Gzip and GPG transforms compose as pipelines. Attach them to reads, writes, or cross-backend transfers. The infer_pipeline helper reads file extensions and applies the right transforms automatically — .csv.gz gets decompressed, .csv.gz.gpg gets decrypted then decompressed.

Copy from S3 to local, local to another S3 bucket, HTTP to S3 — with transforms applied in flight. The source and destination can be any supported backend. Compression and encryption compose into the transfer pipeline.

Eight storage protocols — Read, Write, List, Delete, Metadata, Copy, Directory, Connection — each independently implementable. A backend picks which capabilities it supports. The facade dispatches based on what's available. Adding a new storage backend means implementing the protocols that matter for your use case.

use_cases.title: The multi-cloud data pipeline
use_cases.story: A pipeline reads compressed data from S3, processes it, and writes results to a different cloud provider. The storage facade handles both ends. Transforms decompress on read and compress on write. The pipeline code doesn't know or care which cloud the data lives on.

use_cases.title: The encrypted data lake
use_cases.story: Sensitive data lands GPG-encrypted in S3. Analytics pipelines read it through the storage facade with automatic decryption. Processed results write back encrypted. The encryption is a transform pipeline, not application code — it composes with any read or write operation.

use_cases.title: The migration that doesn't touch application code
use_cases.story: An organisation migrates from AWS S3 to Cloudflare R2. The application code calls the same storage facade methods. The settings class changes its flavour field. The migration is a configuration change.
